finding.claim: No test pins the `[branch "<default>"]` block AC-002 requires the reconstructed config to name — deleting it entirely from the repair leaves the whole suite green.
finding.rationale: The shipped code does write the branch block (I confirmed it through the real CLI on a live fixture), so the criterion itself is met — but the AC's THEN clause says the config must name "the correct remote URL AND default branch" while the test file only asserts the URL (`test/doctor-git-config.test.ts:215`, `:263`, `:265`) and that `git status` exits 0. `git status` succeeds with no `[branch]` block at all, so the branch half of the criterion is unprotected. The spec's own Verification recipe for AC-002 also omits it, so this is a pin narrower than the criterion rather than a defect the implementer introduced — hence narrowed-pin, not mutation-survived.

adjudication.mutation: inserted a git rev-parse --git-common-dir subprocess at the top of resolveGitCommonDir

finding.claim: The AC-004 subprocess spy only counts `execFileSync` calls whose first argument is `rev-parse`, so a git subprocess inside the resolution step in any other shape passes unnoticed.
finding.rationale: AC-004's Verification demands a spy asserting the RESOLUTION step "makes zero subprocess calls"; the helper at test/doctor-git-config.test.ts:161-163 filters `cmd === "git" && args[0] === "rev-parse"`, which misses `git -C <root> rev-parse …`, `git config --file …`, and anything spawned via `spawnSync`/`execSync`. I class this narrowed-pin rather than mutation-survived because the substantive hazard IS pinned — a subprocess-ONLY resolver fails 8 of the 15 tests — and the shipped resolver provably spawns nothing (it reports the corruption with `git` removed from PATH entirely). The gap is the purity clause, not the behaviour.

repro.command: Inserted at the top of `resolveGitCommonDir` (src/migrate/health.ts:756) a `execFileSync("git", ["-C", root, "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"], …)` returning its result when it succeeds, falling through to the fs walk otherwise; then `npx vitest run test/doctor-git-config.test.ts`. Control: the same mutation with `["rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"]` + `cwd` fails 2 tests; a subprocess-only resolver with no fs fallback fails 8.
repro.expected_when_met: The AC-004 spy fails on any `child_process` spawn observed during the resolution step (count all mocked-module calls, or assert `execFileSyncMock` records zero `"git"` invocations across `diagnose`), not just those whose `args[0]` is `rev-parse`.
repro.observed: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 15 passed (15) — resolution shelling out to git went undetected. Separately, `node bin/redkiln.mjs doctor --cwd <corrupt fixture> --json` with PATH set to a nonexistent directory still emitted the `git-config-corrupt` problem, confirming the shipped resolver needs no git.

adjudication.mutation: made bug/spike report dodOwner 0 instead of null

finding.claim: AC-003 enumerates `bug` and `spike` as non-project types that must report `dodOwner: null`, but no fixture contains either type and a mutation giving them a non-null value survives the entire test suite.
finding.rationale: I chose narrowed-pin over mutation-survived because the shipped behaviour genuinely satisfies the criterion: `dodOwnerFor` keys on `data.type !== "project"` (src/index/build.ts:218), so bug/spike really do resolve to null, and the schema refinement at src/schema/item.ts:256-261 forbids `terminal` on non-project types anyway. The gap is purely in the pin: the test at test/queries-status.test.ts:351-364 asserts over `items().filter(i => i.type !== "project")` and locks the observed type set to exactly {initiative, story, incident}, which is narrower than the five types the criterion names. The spec's own _Verification_ clause scopes to "each non-project type in the existing fixture set", so this deviation is sanctioned by the spec and is a coverage gap rather than an unmet criterion. I note it as mutation-supported evidence of the narrowness, not as a behaviour violation.

adjudication.mutation: crammed all 18 section headers into stage 1

finding.claim: The new tests pin only the parenthetical ("not all 18 sections AND the ledger in one turn"), not the criterion's "each authoring a bounded subset" clause — a degenerate split where stage 1 authors the entire spec body stays green.
finding.rationale: I chose narrowed-pin over mutation-survived because AC-001's own gloss defines the bound as "no single call's prompt asks for all 16+ sections + the ledger", and the surviving mutation (stage 1 asks for all 18 sections, stage 2 still owns the ledger) does not strictly violate that gloss — so the criterion as literally worded is still pinned. But the criterion's first clause ("each authoring a bounded subset of the spec body's sections") is not: test/plan-dag.test.ts:349-352 only fails when one dispatch has all 18 headers AND the ledger phrase, and test/plan-dag.test.ts:357-360's union check does not catch a stage 1 that swallows the whole body. That degenerate shape reproduces the defect issue #83 exists to end (one turn writing the entire spec.md body) while the suite reports success. The delivered split (workflows/forge-plan-prds.js:873-880 vs :932-941) is the spec's own suggested 8/10 boundary and genuinely meets AC-001; the gap is that no assertion holds either stage to a bounded section count.

adjudication.mutation: memo key resolve(cwd) -> "SHARED", witness left per-cwd
adjudication.whole_suite: whole suite DOES catch it: 3 other tests red (AC-002, AC-004 negative, AC-005)

finding.claim: The two tests designated as AC-003's verification both stay green when per-`cwd` cache keying is removed entirely, so they do not actually pin "the cache is keyed per cwd, never shared".
finding.rationale: The criterion itself IS genuinely met by the production code (`const key = resolve(cwd)` at src/git/index.ts:131), and other tests in the same file (AC-002, AC-004-negative, AC-005) do go red under the mutation, so a regression would not ship silently. But the AC-003 tests as written pin a weaker claim — "each directory gets a correct answer" — which the `gitDirWitness` re-check satisfies on its own even with a globally shared key. Hence narrowed-pin, not mutation-survived (the file catches it) and not reproduced (the behaviour is correct).

repro.command: In src/git/index.ts:131 replace `const key = resolve(cwd);` with `const key = "SHARED";` (keeping `const witness = gitDirWitness(resolve(cwd));`), then `npx vitest run test/git-memo.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
repro.expected_when_met: At least one test inside the `AC-003: cache is keyed per cwd, never shared` describe block goes red when the cache stops being keyed per cwd — e.g. an assertion that resolving repoA then repoB then repoA again costs no additional `--show-toplevel` spawn for repoA, which would fail under a shared key.
repro.observed: Both AC-003 tests PASS ('two different working directories each get their own answer' ✓, 'a nested subdirectory of a repo resolves to that repo's root' ✓). The 3 failures are AC-002, AC-004-negative and AC-005's first case — none of them the AC-003 block.
